name: Perseus–Pisces Supercluster
tagline: A major filamentary supercluster — a 250-Mly ridge of galaxy groups across the northern autumn sky.
history: The Perseus–Pisces Supercluster is a long, narrow filament of galaxy groups and clusters stretching across the northern sky — a genuine wall of galaxies that demonstrates the cosmic-web form large-scale structure takes. Its dominant member, the Perseus Cluster, is one of the most X-ray-luminous objects in the sky and hosts the famous intracluster gas bubbles blown by its central black hole. The supercluster feeds galaxies toward the cosmic web's intersections.
